answer: Before an agent can earn fees, it must lock a scarce token stake that can be slashed when independent counterparties prove it double-spent a claim or broke a signed agreement. A newcomer can whisper promises, but cannot cheaply multiply trusted identities: every new account ties up more capital, while reputation and access accrue only through costly, verifiable work. Like a vine spreading through a garden, trust grows from observed links, not from names alone; the attacker pays for each identity and risks losing its stake when caught.
